detail.longDescription: arXiv:2611.14204v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scientific computing is under increasing pressure to adapt to HPC hardware that is shaped by AI workloads. In these modern ecosystems, extracting reasonable performance without investing major engineering effort is a central issue for domain scientists. Correctness constraints and intricate reference implementations represent further impediments to development. Instead of using a double-precision implementation as a reference, considering the underlying scientific problem directly opens more opportunities for performance improvements when updating and rewriting applications. We take seven different portability frameworks---covering pragma-based, DSL, and data-centric approaches---and evaluate them on a microphysics kernel of the ICON climate model. Our performance benchmarks show that each different HPC system benefits from a different combination of optimizations, so we develop the measure of framework expressivity to gauge how easily each framework can customize portable implementations in this way.
